description:
The Espresso/Greybeam gateway plan (/Users/joe/.jcode/scratch/espresso-greybeam-plan-v2.md) adds a `gateway` label and per-query execution_engine to the Snowflake and Databricks adapters separately. Baseline guards, tpc_compliant=false, cost suppression and identity are cross-cutting, so the gateway concept belongs in core (ADR D9) and the adapters only supply connection mechanics.

Work:
1. Manifest capability `gateways` {name: {routes_to: {engine_name: {class}}, requires_host: bool}}; `custom` requires a host; `native` is accepted and recorded as no gateway. Snowflake declares espresso, greybeam (routes_to snowflake=standard, duckdb=delegated) and custom; Databricks declares espresso and custom.
2. Core `gateway` setting: CLI --gateway and config key, validated by one core function (not exposed through MCP per ADR D10); gateway connection options (gateway_host, gateway_port, gateway_protocol, gateway_ca_bundle, gateway_ocsp_fail_open, allow_insecure_gateway) registered only on declaring platforms with connection security class.
3. Results: platform.gateway{name, routed}; queries[].execution_engine limited to routes_to names plus `unknown`; platform.execution_engine.observed=mixed when queries differ; tpc_compliant=false whenever routed.
4. Core variants_comparable(a, b) over (deployment, requested engine, gateway), used by benchbox/cli/commands/compare.py, benchbox/core/results/regression_policy.py and analytics baseline selection; it replaces the plan's adapter-level is_native_run.
5. Update docs/development/new-platform-acceptance-checklist.md with the gateway section.
